name: De tai chanh
summary: Dê tái chanh is rare mountain goat dressed with lime, eaten wrapped in sung leaf and dipped in soy sauce. The meat is firm, because the goats climb the limestone. On a Tam Coc day it is the 11:45 lunch with cơm cháy and dê nướng, after Tam Coc, Bích Động, and Thái Vi. A 13 November 2020 provincial goat note describes thin slices with a thick lean part and the skin, passed through boiling water, then mixed with nước cốt chanh, gừng, tỏi, ớt, tiêu, and shredded lá chanh, and does not mention Tam Coc. The 20 October 2023 culture office still places tái dê in the city or the old capital.
origin: Ninh Bình. The culture page names it among the dê núi dishes on the roads toward the sights.
howToEat: Eat it with sung leaves, dipped in soy sauce.

Also eaten with kẹp chuối xanh, sả, and sung quả, and chấm tương bần. On a Tam Coc day the plate is named beside cơm cháy and dê nướng. A city method uses toasted sesame, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, ginger, and tương gừng.
where: The roads and lanes toward Tràng An, Hoa Lư, and Bái Đính.
A local restaurant on a Tam Coc day, after Tam Coc, Bích Động, and Thái Vi. The lunch time is 11:45.

seoDescription: Dê tái chanh in Ninh Bình, eaten with sung leaves and soy sauce, on the roads toward the karst sights.
